message.reasoning_content: Describe the case: Richardson iteration state += (b - A x) with step size 1, converges for eigenvalues in (0,2). Eigenvalues go up to 1.75 < 2, smallest 0.03125. Convergence rate per eigenvalue: |1-λ|; for λ=0.03125, factor 0.96875; 64 steps gives 0.96875^64 ≈ e^(-2) ≈ 0.135. Hmm, that might exceed 8% error. Compute: (1-0.03125)^64. ln(0.96875)≈-0.031748, ×64=-2.0319, e^-2.03≈0.131. But error is weighted by projection of rhs onto that eigenvector and relative to ||x||. x component along λ=0.03125 eigenvalue is amplified by 1/λ=32 relative to rhs component. So relative error contribution ≈ 0.131 * ... actually error along e = |1-λ|^64 * b_e / λ, x component = b_e/λ, so relative ≈0.131 for that mode. That exceeds 0.08. Also λ=0.0625: (0.9375)^64 = e^(-4.07)=0.017. So dominant error mode λ=0.03125 with ~13% residual. But also λ=1.75: |1-1.75|=0.75, negligible. So likely fails. That's for Skeptic.
